study type: Prospective longitudinal cohort with nested case-control
outcome: Laeverin protein concentration in maternal plasma
Laeverin protein expression in placental tissue
Laeverin levels in umbilical artery and vein serum
cohort: The study included 53 healthy pregnant women, 15 women who later developed preeclampsia, 10 healthy non-pregnant premenopausal women, 10 menopausal women, 11 men, and neonates from healthy (n=38) and preeclamptic (n=14) mothers.
finding: Maternal plasma laeverin levels decrease with advancing gestation in normal pregnancies, and lower levels at 22-24 weeks might be associated with the development of preeclampsia, while laeverin levels were higher in preeclamptic placentas but lower in umbilical venous samples of neonates from preeclamptic mothers compared to healthy controls.
